title: Kingdom of Gordyene
capsule: Gordyene (Corduene) was a small mountainous kingdom north of the Tigris headwaters in what is now southeastern Turkey, inhabited by the Carduchi and lying in contested borderland between the Armenian kingdom, the Parthian empire, and Rome. Lucullus secured it from Tigranes the Great around 69 BCE, and Pompey confirmed Roman suzerainty in 66 BCE, though the region changed hands repeatedly; Trajan briefly incorporated it during his Mesopotamian campaigns of 114–117 CE. The territory was definitively absorbed into the Sasanian empire in the third century CE following the conquests of Ardashir I and Shapur I, with the 260 CE date coinciding with Shapur I's decisive campaigns against Rome.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general location of Gordyene is consistently attested in Strabo, Tacitus, and Pliny, but precise boundaries of this small mountain kingdom and its internal political structure are poorly documented.
